name: KY-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 partisan lean in a deeply red northern Kentucky district
Open seat with no incumbent, but Republican nominee heavily favored
Polymarket prices Democratic win at about 1 percent
Democratic nominee raised under $100,000 with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean and the absence of any competitive signals make this a Safe R seat despite the open seat created by Massie's renomination loss. The Democratic nominee's minimal fundraising and Polymarket pricing near 1 percent confirm no credible path for an upset.
model.watch: A divisive Republican primary aftermath or a late scandal involving Gallrein could tighten the race, but the structural lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Thomas Massie (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Kentucky's 4th District is an open seat after Thomas Massie lost renomination, with Republican Ed Gallrein emerging as the nominee. The district carries an R+18 partisan lean, among the more Republican-leaning seats in the country, and no expert raters list the general election as competitive. Polymarket prices the Democratic nominee's chances at roughly 1 percent.

Democrat Melissa Strange has raised under $100,000 with no outside spending on her behalf, while heavy outside money has flowed into the Republican primary contest. A Libertarian is also on the ballot but is not a factor. The fundamentals point to the seat remaining comfortably in Republican hands.
